metadata.name: The Exodus Route
metadata.description: Israel's journey from Egypt through the wilderness to Canaan (~1446 BC)

properties.name: Rameses (Goshen)
properties.description: The Israelites set out from Rameses with about 600,000 men plus families, ending 430 years of sojourn in Egypt.

properties.name: Succoth
properties.description: Israel's first stop after leaving Rameses; they baked unleavened cakes since there was no time for bread to rise.

properties.name: Etham
properties.description: At Etham on the edge of the wilderness, God led Israel by a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.

properties.name: Pi-hahiroth (Red Sea Crossing)
properties.description: God parted the Red Sea; Israel crossed on dry ground, and Pharaoh's pursuing army was drowned when the waters returned.

properties.name: Marah
properties.description: The people could not drink the bitter waters of Marah; God showed Moses a tree which, when thrown in, made the water sweet.

properties.name: Elim
properties.description: At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and the people camped there by the waters.

properties.name: Wilderness of Sin
properties.description: Israel grumbled about food; God provided quail in the evening and manna each morning — except on the Sabbath.

properties.name: Mount Sinai (Horeb)
properties.description: God descended on the mountain in fire, thunder, and lightning, and gave the Ten Commandments and the Mosaic Law to Israel.

properties.name: Kadesh-barnea
properties.description: The twelve spies returned from Canaan; ten gave a fearful report. Israel rebelled and was condemned to 40 years in the wilderness.

properties.name: Oboth / Punon
properties.description: God sent fiery serpents as judgment for Israel's complaints. Moses lifted a bronze serpent on a pole — all who looked at it lived.

properties.name: Plains of Moab
properties.event_name: Moses Views Canaan; Death of Moses
properties.description: From Mount Nebo, Moses viewed the Promised Land he could not enter. He died at 120 years old; Joshua was commissioned to lead Israel across the Jordan.
